definitions.gloss: an iron pot or pan — cookware made of cast iron or wrought iron, valued for even heat retention and durability
definitions.explanation: Refers to any cooking pot or pan made of iron. Often used in Japanese cooking for dishes that benefit from high heat or long simmering, such as すき{焼|や}き or {餃子|ぎょうざ}. Also commonly seen at restaurants as a serving vessel that keeps food hot at the table.

examples.japanese: {鉄鍋|てつなべ}で{料理|りょうり}する。
examples.english: I cook in an iron pan.

examples.japanese: {鉄鍋|てつなべ}は{熱|ねつ}がよく{伝|つた}わる。
{祖母|そぼ}から{譲|ゆず}り{受|う}けた{鉄鍋|てつなべ}を{今|いま}でも{使|つか}っている。
examples.english: I still use the iron pot I inherited from my grandmother.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}の{餃子|ぎょうざ}は{熱々|あつあつ}の{鉄鍋|てつなべ}ごと{運|はこ}ばれてくる。
examples.english: At this restaurant, the gyoza are brought out sizzling hot in the iron pan itself.

notes:
Compound of {鉄|てつ} ("iron") + {鍋|なべ} ("pot, pan"). Refers to cookware made of iron — including skillets, Dutch-oven-style pots, and the Chinese-style shallow pans used for {餃子|ぎょうざ}.

USAGE:
- The same object can also be called a {鉄製|てつせい}の{鍋|なべ} ("iron-made pot") in more formal writing.
- At restaurants, the phrase {鉄鍋|てつなべ}ごと means "pan and all" — the dish is served in the hot pan itself.
- Iron pans require seasoning and careful maintenance; this is often discussed with the verb {育|そだ}てる ("to raise/season") or {手入|てい}れする ("to maintain").

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鉄鍋|てつなべ}で{焼|や}く: to cook (sear, fry) in an iron pan
- {鉄鍋|てつなべ}{料理|りょうり}: iron-pan cuisine
- {鉄鍋|てつなべ}{餃子|ぎょうざ}: gyoza served in an iron pan
- {鉄鍋|てつなべ}を{育|そだ}てる: to season/break in an iron pan

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {鍋|なべ}: general word for pot or pan — any material.
- {土鍋|どなべ}: earthenware pot — used for hot pot dishes like {鍋物|なべもの}.
- {中華鍋|ちゅうかなべ}: wok — a Chinese-style iron pan.
- フライパン: frying pan — usually implies a modern pan with a handle, often non-stick.
